rows.label: Nursing facility / total paid claims (DMS, SFY 2024)
Nursing facility paid / DMS SFY 2024 total ($18.5B)

measures.methodNote: Nursing facility FFS spending ($1,555.5M, CMS-64 via KFF, FFY 2024) / total KY Medicaid spending ($18,302M, CMS-64 via MACPAC Exhibit 16, FFY 2024) = 8.5%. Of benefits only ($17,879M) = 8.7%. Including ICF/IID ($1,723.6M) = 9.4%. DMS's own SFY 2024 claims view shows nursing facilities at 9.71% of total paid claims/encounters ($1,399.1M), but that base (about $14.4B) excludes Medicare premiums, directed payments and other non-claim spending; against DMS's stated $18.5B SFY 2024 total it is 7.6%. CHECK ON ADAM MATHER'S FIGURE: the fee-for-service part is CONFIRMED. Nursing facility care is carved out of managed care in Kentucky: residents of a nursing facility for more than 30 days are not enrolled in an MCO (907 KAR 17:010 Sec. 1(3)(a)); the 2026-2028 enacted budget states 'Recipients in long term care facilities and waiver programs are excluded from managed care enrollment'; DMS lists long-term care under Fee for Service; MCOs paid only $0.48M of $1,399M SFY 2024 nursing facility claims. The dollar figure is somewhat HIGH: nursing facility FFS is about $1.4-1.6B (not $2B) of about $18.3-18.5B total (FFY/SFY 2024), roughly 8.5% (range 7.6%-9.7% depending on base), not 10%. The $2B is approached only if ICF/IID and mental-health institutions are added (institutional LTSS $1.76B). 'About $20B' matches SFY 2025 total DMS spending ($20.59B actual), but no SFY 2025 nursing facility figure was found; at the FFY 2024 nursing facility level the SFY 2025 share would be about 7.7%.

measures.label: Why spending changed: fewer members vs. higher cost per member
measures.methodNote: Spending S = MM x P (member-months x PMPM). Midpoint (Shapley) split: enrollment effect = (MM1 - MM0) x (P0 + P1)/2; per-member cost effect = (P1 - P0) x (MM0 + MM1)/2; the two sum exactly to S1 - S0. MM0 = 18,850,200, MM1 = 17,309,892, P0 = $864.65, P1 = $1,032.86. Enrollment effect = -$1,461.4M; per-member cost effect = +$3,041.3M; total = +$1,579.9M (+9.7%). Log form: ln(S1/S0) 9.25% = ln(MM1/MM0) -8.52% + ln(P1/P0) +17.78%. Context, not quantified here: FFY 2023 included continuous enrollment through March 2023, so the post-unwinding mix of members differs; directed payments flow through capitation.

measures.methodNote: FTE estimate = DMS personnel costs / fully loaded cost per state employee. Loaded cost = average salary x (1 + KERS non-hazardous employer rate + employer FICA + Medicare) + 12 x employer health contribution + 12 x employer life insurance = $60,674 x (1 + 0.5762 + 0.062 + 0.0145) + 12 x $1,016.40 + 12 x $1.00 = $112,485. FTE = $211,675,519 / $112,485 = 1,882. CAVEATS: (1) This is an UPPER BOUND on state employees: Kentucky's 'Personnel Costs' expenditure class also includes personal service contracts (outside contractors), which are not separately shown for DMS, so true DMS headcount is likely well below this figure. (2) Salary is the all-agency KERS non-hazardous average, not a DMS-specific average. (3) Health contribution uses the 2026 plan-year LivingWell PPO single employer rate; family coverage would raise loaded cost and lower the estimate. (4) The 57.62% KERS rate is the budget planning rate from OSBD's 2024-26 defined calculations. No published authorized-position or FTE count for DMS was found in the Budget of the Commonwealth (2024-26 or 2026-28 Volume I) or LRC documents.

Budget asOf dates are approximate (biennium start / April 2026 passage).
